# Awesome Agentic Trading

[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge-flat.svg)](https://awesome.re)
[![validate](https://github.com/rio26/awesome-agentic-trading/actions/workflows/validate.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rio26/awesome-agentic-trading/actions/workflows/validate.yml)
[![last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/rio26/awesome-agentic-trading?style=flat-square&label=updated)](https://github.com/rio26/awesome-agentic-trading/commits/main)

The watchlist for LLM trading agents: the agents themselves, the MCP servers that feed and execute for them, prediction-market bots, the guardrails and evals around them, and the public record of what went wrong.

![Agentic trading landscape: data, decision, execution, risk, evaluation](docs/landscape.svg)

**How to read this list.** Sections follow the pipeline in the diagram: what an agent sees, how it decides, how it trades, what stops it, and how you know it works. Every GitHub entry shows live star and last-commit badges, and tags for market (`equities`, `crypto`, `prediction-markets`, ...) and mode (`live`, `paper`, `research`, `library`). Entries with no commits in six months are marked, not deleted; a weekly job keeps that honest.

**What is not here.** General quant libraries, broker APIs without an agent angle, and courses on algorithmic trading: see [Related lists](#related-lists). Closed-source products and paid signal services are out of scope.

> **Not investment advice.** Everything listed can lose money, and the `live` entries can lose it quickly. Read [Incidents](#incidents--postmortems) before you connect an agent to a funded account.
